Repository: django/django
Base commit: 74fd233b1433da8c68de636172ee1c9c6d1c08c9
### Issue
Django adds spurious "/" prefix to settings.STATIC_URL="http://server/"
Description
	 
		(last modified by Adam Hooper)
	 
Here's a piece of settings from a totally reasonable, sensible, okay Docker integration-test environment
STATIC_URL = "http://minio/static/"
Django 3.1 will implicitly add "/" to the URL, so my URLs look like /http://minio/static/images/app-icons/favicon.ico
The features and bugs that interact here:
commit c574bec, adding feature #25598, prepends SCRIPT_NAME to STATIC_URL when STATIC_URL isn't a URL.
bug #9202 and #25418: according to Django, "​http://minio/static/" isn't a valid URL. (It is.)
Top me, the easiest fix is to address #9202 / #25418. Or to make STATIC_URL use some logic that is different from URLValidator.

### Candidate patch
```diff
diff --git a/django/contrib/staticfiles/handlers.py b/django/contrib/staticfiles/handlers.py
index 44fef0722d..1b29262fbe 100644
--- a/django/contrib/staticfiles/handlers.py
+++ b/django/contrib/staticfiles/handlers.py
@@ -35,7 +35,11 @@ class StaticFilesHandlerMixin:
         * the host is provided as part of the base_url
         * the request's path isn't under the media path (or equal)
         """
-        return path.startswith(self.base_url[2]) and not self.base_url[1]
+        # Reconstruct the full URL if base_url is a full URL
+        if self.base_url.scheme and self.base_url.netloc:  # scheme and netloc are present
+            full_url = f"{self.base_url.scheme}://{self.base_url.netloc}{self.base_url.path}"
+            return path.startswith(full_url)
+        return path.startswith(self.base_url.path)
 
     def file_path(self, url):
         """
@@ -68,7 +72,12 @@ class StaticFilesHandler(StaticFilesHandlerMixin, WSGIHandler):
     """
     def __init__(self, application):
         self.application = application
-        self.base_url = urlparse(self.get_base_url())
+        base_url = self.get_base_url()
+        # Ensure STATIC_URL is treated as a URL when it starts with http:// or https://
+        if base_url.startswith(('http://', 'https://')):
+            self.base_url = urlparse(base_url)
+        else:
+            self.base_url = ('', '', base_url, '', '', '')
         super().__init__()
 
     def __call__(self, environ, start_response):
@@ -84,7 +93,12 @@ class ASGIStaticFilesHandler(StaticFilesHandlerMixin, ASGIHandler):
     """
     def __init__(self, application):
         self.application = application
-        self.base_url = urlparse(self.get_base_url())
+        base_url = self.get_base_url()
+        # Ensure STATIC_URL is treated as a URL when it starts with http:// or https://
+        if base_url.startswith(('http://', 'https://')):
+            self.base_url = urlparse(base_url)
+        else:
+            self.base_url = ('', '', base_url, '', '', '')
 
     async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send):
         # Only even look at HTTP requests
diff --git a/reproduce_bug.py b/reproduce_bug.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..562c42ff27
--- /dev/null
+++ b/reproduce_bug.py
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+import django
+from django.conf import settings
+from django.templatetags.static import static
+
+settings.configure(
+    DEBUG=True,
+    STATIC_URL="http://minio/static/",
+    SECRET_KEY='a-very-bad-secret-key',
+    ALLOWED_HOSTS=[]
+)
+
+django.setup()
+
+# Attempt to output a static URL
+print(static('images/app-icons/favicon.ico'))
+
+# Add a message to indicate the script completed successfully
+print("Script completed successfully, no errors.")

```

parsed.reason: The patch correctly addresses the issue by ensuring that STATIC_URL is treated as a URL when it starts with 'http://' or 'https://'. The additional test script helps verify the functionality.
